messages:
maria: Customer reports ~8% of audit events missing from our SIEM export for tenant-42 over the last 24h. They saw gaps in Splunk around 2026-03-15 09:00-12:00 UTC. Forwarder manifest in S3: s3://redwood-audit-exports/prod/tenant-42/2026-03-15/manifest.json. Sample missing event IDs: evt_8a12c, evt_b9f3d, evt_c102e. They also see intermittent 403s in forwarder logs. Can eng/security triage? :eyes:
akshay: Can you paste the specific forwarder log lines and the manifest entry for one of the missing blobs? Also did the customer try a replay or re-download of the manifest? Any KMS errors in the logs?
maria: Pasting snippet:
``
[2026-03-15T09:11:03Z] forwarder/tenant=tenant-42 INFO uploading batch key=2026-03-15/part-0003.gz.enc size=1.2MB
[2026-03-15T09:11:04Z] forwarder ERROR upload failed status=403 response="Forbidden: signature mismatch"
[2026-03-15T09:11:04Z] forwarder WARN retrying batch id=part-0003 attempt=1
```
Manifest entry for part-0003:
``
{"key":"2026-03-15/part-0003.gz.enc","checksum":"sha256:aa11...","kms_key_id":"arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/abcd-efgh-2026v2"}
```
They tried a small replay using the console replay tool, got: `decrypting blob: hsm: unauthorized`.
akshay: Signature mismatch on upload + HSM decrypt unauthorized on replay — looks like a key/signing rotation issue. Did we rotate any KMS aliases or push forwarder signing keys around 2026-03-15?
ingrid: We did a scheduled KMS alias rotation for `alias/redwood-audit-prod` on 2026-03-15 08:50 UTC (small safety window). New key id is `key/abcd-efgh-2026v2` (matches manifest). HSM team also pushed firmware updates at 08:45 UTC. Some forwarders might not have picked up the new signing token; the replay tool may be using a cached HSM wrapper key.
lisa: I grepped the forwarder fleet logs — ~12 forwarder instances reported 403s between 09:10-09:20 UTC, all in us-east-1 AZ b. Example from forwarder-7:
``
2026-03-15T09:11:04Z forwarder-7 error upload 403 "signature verification failed: nonce mismatch"
```
akshay: Nonce mismatch suggests the forwarder signing token disagrees with the ingest verification table. Did we partially roll the signing token in Vault or in config-service?
ingrid: Vault shows a rotation event at 08:40 UTC for `audit-forwarder-signing`. Config-service reports a partial deploy at 08:48 — some instances failed to apply and were restarted later. The SIEM verification keys were not changed.
akshay: That fits: partial signing token rollout combined with HSM wrapper changes -> some forwarders uploaded batches signed with the new HMAC while the ingest endpoint only accepted the old HMAC. Replay tool failing with `hsm: unauthorized` indicates the wrapper wasn't re-registered for those instances.
maria: Customer asked if data is unrecoverable and requested repro steps + ETA. They want the missing batches replayed into their Splunk index.
akshay: Ops repro steps to validate and reproduce locally:
1) On a forwarder instance in the affected AZ, tail forwarder logs and trigger a push: `sudo -u forwarder /usr/local/bin/forwarder push --tenant tenant-42 --batch 2026-03-15/part-0003.gz.enc`
2) Check HMAC key metadata in `/etc/forwarder/config.yaml` and compare to `vault read secret/audit-forwarder-signing`
3) On the ingest side: `SELECT key_id, active FROM signing_keys WHERE service='siem-ingest';`
4) For ops-only KMS test: `aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://part-0003.gz.enc --key-id arn:aws:kms:... --output text --query Plaintext | base64 --decode` — watch for `hsm: unauthorized`. If you see that, escalate to HSM.
ingrid: I'll ask HSM to validate cluster wrapper keys and confirm whether wrapped keys were re-wrapped after the firmware push. I'll also audit config-service rollout logs to identify the forwarders that missed the signing token.
lisa: I started a narrow staging replay for tenant-42 for 2026-03-15T09:00-09:30. It failed with `403 signature verification failed` for 5/12 batches. Those 5 map to forwarder instances that restarted during the deploy window.
maria: Fast-fix options for customer:
- Re-push signing token config to the 5 failed forwarders (fast).
- Ask HSM to rewrap/confirm wrapper keys for those instances (slower).
- Once tokens/wrappers are reconciled, perform targeted replay of the failed S3 keys into the customer's Splunk.
akshay: Shortest path: re-push config to the 5 failed forwarders, then retry replay. Risk: if HSM wrapper for those instances was never registered, decrypts will still fail; logs suggest most failures are signature mismatches, not decrypt failures on upload, so start with config push.
ingrid: Agreed. I'll coordinate ops to reapply the signing token to the failed forwarders and follow up with HSM for wrapper sanity. Opening an incident for tracking.
sre-bot: Incident INC-2026-042 created by ingrid — topic: audit-export partial delivery due to HSM/config-rollout mismatch. Severity: P2. Assignees: akshay, lisa, ingrid, maria.
maria: I'll update the customer with the incident link, manifest references, and ETA. Preliminary ETA: 2-4 hours if ops can re-push config now and HSM confirms wrapper keys; 8-24 hours if HSM rewraps are required. We believe the S3 blobs exist and are recoverable.
akshay: I'll lead the config re-push and signature verification checks. Ingrid — please ping HSM for wrapper confirmation. Lisa — continue replay to staging and capture failing S3 keys so we can target them after fix.
lingering action items:
- ingrid: config-service rollout audit + HSM ping (INC-2026-042)
- akshay: reapply signing token to 5 instances, verify signature header and key id on upload
- lisa: collect list of failed S3 keys and record which forwarder instance uploaded each key
- maria: customer comms and manifest + sample event IDs attached to incident
- HSM team: confirm wrapper key registration for affected forwarder hostnames
notes:
- Root cause likely a race between Vault/config-service rotation and HSM firmware wrapper push causing a cohort of forwarders to operate with mismatched signing wrappers/keys.
- Recovery plan: re-push signing token to failed forwarders, verify signature acceptance, run targeted replay of specific S3 keys to customer's Splunk.
maria: Thanks team, keeping customer updated. :thumbsup:
